interactions.summary: Jiang walks the class through the mirror experiment in everyday terms, concludes that distance does not dim reflected brightness, and declares the whole scene a scientific debate in which reason refutes a merely logical appearance.
The reader delivers Beatrice's transition: Dante's error has been melted away like snow in warm rays, and she is now ready to offer a new living light.

Jiang asks why Beatrice bothers with a long Socratic dialogue instead of simply stating the truth, and the class answers that the sequence stabilizes imagination, dramatizes the difference between knowledge and imagination, and lets the reader reason through Dante's ascent.
interactions.speaker_attribution: Jiang-led classroom exchange with multiple student answers

claims.claim: Jiang says the mirror experiment shows that even if one mirror is vastly farther away, its reflected image would still be equally bright, so depth alone cannot explain the moon's darker regions.
Jiang concludes that Beatrice uses logic and reason to refute the class's own logic and reason, keeping the heavenly dispute legible as a science debate.
The quoted passage says Beatrice's refutation strips Dante's mind bare of error the way warm sunlight strips snow of its color and cold, preparing him for a brighter truth.
claims.temporal_scope: Quoted literary material read aloud on 2026-06-15.

claims.claim: A student proposes that Beatrice must convince Dante he is really in heaven, because if his imagination fails to hold the experience together he would fall back into ordinary waking life.
Jiang rejects treating the dialogue as a literal transcript of heaven and pushes the class to ask why Dante the poet structures the exchange this way.
A student argues that Dante structures the scene to show the difference between knowledge and imagination rather than merely to narrate heavenly facts.
Another student says the extended dialogue lets readers reason their way through Dante's experience instead of being handed a conclusion without participation.

signature_moments.moment: A mirror ten feet away and a mirror ten thousand kilometers away are forced into the same brightness.
signature_moments.source_phrase: no matter how far it is from you, it will still be as bright
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It preserves the concrete empirical image by which Jiang collapses the cavity theory and keeps the packet from drifting into abstraction.

signature_moments.moment: Beatrice's correction is imagined as snow losing both its whiteness and its cold under warm light.
signature_moments.source_phrase: your mind left bare of error
signature_moments.why_it_matters: This is the packet's most vivid poetic turn: error is not just disproven but melted away to make room for a more living illumination.

signature_moments.moment: Jiang stops the class from treating Beatrice as a lecturer and asks why truth takes the form of Socratic dialogue at all.
signature_moments.source_phrase: why is she engaging in this dialogue, this Socratic dialogue
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It marks the shift from solving a lunar puzzle to asking what kind of education Dante thinks real understanding requires.

glossary_terms.definition_or_usage: Jiang's summary for the moon episode, where poetic ascent includes an argument conducted in the idiom of experiment and refutation.
Beatrice's promised new form of illumination after Dante's error has been stripped away.
Jiang's label for the educational process by which Beatrice leads Dante toward truth instead of simply asserting it.

chronology_notes.note: This packet completes the June 15 refutation of the density theory and then pivots into a meta-reading about why Dante stages truth as guided dialogue, without creating cross-source chronology pressure.
